title: Phase 2 — publish the cross-language contract
description: EIGHT CORE GO TESTS read fixtures out of cloud/factory/test/fixtures/ — the dependency runs backwards from what anyone would predict. They are deliberate Go/TS drift detectors: .tick/runners.toml is parsed by internal/herd/config AND re-implemented in cloud/factory/src/{toml,repo-config}.ts, and the fixtures are what stop the two diverging. Same for sandbox worker boot and message context. internal/gatewaytrace/trace_test.go:332-342 pins constants against cloud/factory/src/gateway.ts by convention. Move the fixtures into a versioned artifact both repos consume (skills/ticks/references/runners-config.schema.json is the natural seed) and repoint both test suites at it. A naive extraction relocates these and silently disables eight drift detectors — the likeliest way this project does real damage.
notes:
2026-08-27 11:54 - FROM TICK psh — a THREE-way vocabulary contract now held together only by a comment. Phase 2 should cover it.

The collect verdict and status strings are shared by THREE implementations: internal/herd/collect (local), internal/cloud/collect (cloud, laptop side), and cloud/factory/src/worker-collect.ts (the Worker). Until psh landed, the first two were the SAME TYPE by import, so drift between them was impossible by construction. They are now copies.

The failure mode is silent and it is the worst kind: if NEEDS_CONTEXT or ready-to-merge is re-spelled in one place, a cloud run and a herd run disagree about what happened to the same tick and NOTHING FAILS. The report just quietly means something different.

Symbols in the contract: Verdict, ReadyToMerge, NoCommits, MissingResult, BoundaryViolation, StatusBlocked, StatusNeedsContext, ParseStatus.

AND MORE THAN THE CONSTANTS: the statusLine regexp is part of it too — including the DONE_WITH_CONCERNS-before-DONE alternation order (get that wrong and DONE_WITH_CONCERNS parses as DONE, which is a verdict inversion) and the markdown decoration trim set. A fixture that only pins the four constants would miss both.

The psh implementer considered a parity test in internal/herd/collect importing internal/cloud/collect — legal, since the forbidden direction is the other way — and deliberately left it out rather than inverting the dependency in tests. That option is still open and may be cheaper than a full contract artifact for the Go-to-Go half; the Go-to-TS half needs the artifact regardless.
2026-08-27 12:16 - FROM THE 82h REVIEW — a CLASS observation worth carrying into this epic's scoping, beyond the individual items already filed.

Phase 1 converted FOUR compiler-enforced agreements into comment-enforced ones: the collect verdict strings, the collect status strings, the eight-colour palette, and the herd dashboard key bindings. Each is individually defensible, each is documented at its site, and the reviewer verified all four copies are faithful TODAY (byte-identical values, line-by-line).

The aggregate is what matters: drift surface went up by four, and every one of them fails SILENTLY rather than loudly. That makes this epic's contract artifact load-bearing rather than hygiene — which the spec already says, but it is now literally true rather than anticipatory.

Specifically worth deciding here: whether the herd/factory key-binding agreement is restored via the shared fixture. It was a test that rendered the herd board's real footer and compared bindings; it did not survive the import removal and the keys are now a frozen literal. Both view_test.go and doc.go say so plainly rather than papering over it. Restoring it is low priority — the literal is correct today — but it is the clearest example of the class.
acceptance_criteria: Deliberately breaking cloud/factory/src/toml.ts still fails a Go test, with no test reading a fixture by relative path across the repo boundary. All eight detectors demonstrably still fire — show one failing on purpose. go test ./... and the factory vitest suite green.
